QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_46

question.text: Per Ch 9.4.1, Large ticket-size investors and Accredited Investors in an AIF have been given the right to:

answer.text: Veto any investment made by the manager
Representation on the Investment Management Committee to monitor investment opportunities and risks

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.4.1 Point 3: Large ticket-size and Accredited Investors have been given RIGHT OF REPRESENTATION on the Investment Management Committee to monitor investments. Not veto, not forced redemption. The Trap: Option A overstates — IC members usually have one vote, not veto. Option B violates close-ended structure. Option D sits with the Sponsor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B covers LP rights; XIX-C requires IC governance setup. Manager's Pro-Tip: Define the IMC observer vs voting seat in PPM clearly. Voting seats can trigger conflicts (LP-appointed director might have fiduciary conflicts) — many funds prefer observer-only seats for LPs.
